context: Build into a same-filesystem temporary sibling, close/checkpoint it, reject any remaining WAL, validate a DB-only copy through the same queries the browser needs, and atomically replace the public snapshot only after success. Add deterministic interruption tests around process termination and prior-artifact preservation without relying on timing-sensitive WAL sampling.
description: Fault injection proved that the current invariant can open a 12 KB results.duckdb with a sibling WAL and report success even though the DB copied alone has no results table. A normal production-shaped build closed and checkpointed cleanly, so this is defense in depth rather than a current launch blocker. Make DB-only portability an explicit artifact contract and preserve the last known-good snapshot across interruption.

anti_patterns.dont: merely call CHECKPOINT before the existing invariant
anti_patterns.instead: validate an isolated DB-only artifact and atomically promote it
anti_patterns.why: the invariant would still be capable of replaying a sidecar and artifact publication would remain non-atomic

anti_patterns.dont: use a sleep-and-kill timing assertion as the only regression
anti_patterns.instead: unit-test promotion boundaries and add one bounded process-interruption integration case
anti_patterns.why: WAL timing varies by DuckDB version and host

anti_patterns.instead: build and validate a same-directory temporary snapshot before os.replace
anti_patterns.why: a killed process can expose a partial replacement

preserves.behavior: A failed or interrupted rebuild cannot replace or delete the last known-good published snapshot.
Successful normal builds retain current table/view contents, row counts, read_model_version, and critical-path query performance.
Temporary files are created beside the target for atomic replacement and are cleaned only by exact validated path.
The browser continues to fetch one results.duckdb URL and never depends on a WAL or extra database sidecar.
The invariant validates the serialized artifact the browser receives, not an in-process connection or sibling sidecar state.

prior_art.concept: Keep publication ordered build then invariant then frontend assembly; add no parallel artifact path.
Retain the existing connection lifecycle but redirect output to a temporary publish candidate.
Strengthen the existing schema/content gate with DB-only portability and no-WAL assertions.

verifications.description: Snapshot invariant explicitly rejects WAL sidecars
verifications.expected: Fails on the unfixed tree; exits 0 when the invariant contains an explicit no-WAL artifact check.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/scripts/explorer_pipeline tests/unit/scripts -q
verifications.expected: Normal, isolated-copy, WAL-assisted, and interrupted-promotion cases all pass.

verifications.description: The full Explorer pipeline and smoke test consume the promoted DB alone
verifications.expected: The browser-facing artifact passes without any sibling WAL and retains the expected model version.

work_units.evidence: Code audit confirmed direct public DB unlink/write and WAL-replaying invariant. Contract: browser receives one self-contained results.duckdb; candidate DB and bundle files are staged beside target, old DB remains active until final atomic promotion.
work_units.notes: Define candidate naming, close/checkpoint requirements, forbidden sidecars, DB-only validation, atomic replacement, previous-artifact retention, cleanup ownership, Windows/POSIX replacement behavior, and maximum interruption-test runtime.
work_units.summary: Specify the self-contained snapshot and atomic-promotion contract

work_units.evidence: PR #1483 commit ba08d744a makes DuckDBSnapshotBuilder build into same-directory UUID temp files and os.replace only after connection close; exact candidate and WAL siblings are cleaned on failure.
work_units.notes: Create the candidate beside the target, close DuckDB, fail if a WAL remains, copy/open the DB in isolation, and run schema, metadata, row-count, and required-view probes. Do not touch the target until all checks pass.
work_units.summary: Build and validate a temporary DB-only publish candidate

work_units.evidence: PR #1483 stages bundles and DB under a sibling temp directory, validates the candidate, atomically publishes bundle files and results.duckdb, and cleans stale generated artifacts only after promotion.
work_units.notes: Use an atomic same-filesystem replacement after validation, retain or restore the previous artifact on any failure, and clean only the exact candidate/WAL paths created by this run. Record candidate and final sizes without logging corpus-sensitive values.
work_units.summary: Atomically promote the candidate and preserve rollback

work_units.evidence: PR #1483 adds WAL-sidecar rejection and failed-rebuild preservation tests; 17 focused tests, 312 explorer-pipeline tests, 1392 unit/scripts tests, 23 smoke/build-contract tests all passed.
work_units.notes: Prove a normal build publishes one self-contained DB, a deliberately WAL-assisted tiny DB is rejected, and killing a bounded child before promotion leaves the previous DB byte-identical and never presents the candidate at the public path.
work_units.summary: Add normal, WAL-assisted, and interrupted-build regressions
